_what: THE SCANNER OBLIGATIONS POLICY (owner 2026-11-18, approved 2026-11-24, KDEC-069). What a repository must be scanned for is decided by discovery (what it contains; what it pushes or deploys) and this versioned policy; a scanner token decides only whether a provider can run. Kit-owned and protected (governance-profile.json scanner_floor class). Read by scripts/scanner_obligations.py through .github/actions/scanner-obligations, from the kit at the caller's pinned commit, never from the checkout.
_providers: Each provider lists the coverage aspects it gives and the issue types it detects (closure equivalence). Core providers are ADOPTED by default and their identities are capability-floor identities. External providers (ext-<name>, the KDEC-028 row name) are options until a provider_lifecycle record ADOPTS them in an organisation's copy. An ADOPTED provider that did not run, with no RETIRED record, is UNAVAILABLE whatever its token says.
_lifecycle: provider_lifecycle is append-only history, the last record per provider wins. Retiring a provider is ONE line: {"provider": "ext-x", "state": "RETIRED", "on": "YYYY-MM-DD", "by": "<login>", "reason": "...", "replaced_by": "<provider>"}. Retiring a provider never retires the control: the obligation stays, and what no provider covers is a visible COVERAGE_GAP.
_decisions: coverage_gap_acceptances: {obligation, aspects?, accepted_by, risk_owner, decided_on, expires, reference}; accepted_by must be the risk owner and it lives at most acceptance_max_days. control_retirements: {obligation, decided_by (security), risk_owner, residual_risk_accepted_by (= risk_owner), decided_on, reference}. obligation_exceptions: {obligation, repository, exception_ref, requested_by, approved_by (not the requester, not a bot), expires}; a repository's .kit/obligations.json `remove` is honoured only when it names one of these. The change that adds any of these records needs main-branch approval; the residual risk is accepted by the risk owner named in it.

obligations.why: Every repository can hold a committed credential.
Every repository can declare a dependency with a known vulnerability.
Source code the repository contains is read for flaws.
Infrastructure as code the repository contains is read for misconfiguration.
A Dockerfile the repository contains is read for unsafe build practice.
Workflows the repository contains are read for syntax and for injection and permission flaws.
An image the run builds or pushes is read for vulnerable packages and embedded secrets.
A WordPress site's core, plugins and themes carry their own advisories, which a manifest scan does not see.
A deployed web application is exercised running, in its predecessor environment (never prod).
